Title: Squashed Flat
Chunks: 9,10,11,12,13,14,15,16,17,28,29,30,31,32,53,54,55,56,57
## Examples:
*   _Pokémon the Series_:   
    *    The original series episode "Gluttonous Kabigon! Huge Panic!" (or "Snack Attack!" in the English dub), in which Snorlax would roll over and lay on some of the Pokemon trying to attack him. The sight of a flattened Victreebel trying to walk around while flat, and shrieking at the top of its lungs, is hysterical.   
    *    Happens to Pikachu in the _Advanced Battle_ episode "Solid As A Solrock!" During a Gym Battle set in a planetarium, Pikachu charges Solrock with his Quick Attack, but Solrock moves out of the way, and Pikachu slams right into a model planet. Moments later, Pikachu's flattened form peels out of the crater and drifts to the ground.   
    *    Pikachu suffers this again in the _Black and White_ episode "New Places, Familar Faces"; After James' Amoongus body slams him, he is left flattened in a small crater, and stunned long enough for Team Rocket to capture him.   
    *    In the _Sun and Moon_ episode "Pulling Out The Pokemon Base Pepper!", a Snorlax uses its Z-Move, Pulverizing Pancake, on Team Rocket's Wobuffet, reducing it to, well... a pancake. 

## Examples:
*   _Punirunes (2022)_: In the first episode, Yuka's father accidentally squishes Airun when he is rolling dough for bread. Airun, being a squishy Punirune, isn't hurt by it and reverts to its normal shape afterward.   
*    Ransack and Crumplezone suffer this fate in the _Transformers: Cybertron_ episodes "Race" and "Ambush" (after being dropped on by Dirt Boss in the former, and run over by Metroplex in the latter).   
*   _Voices in the Dark_: This is a danger you face when eating the ridiculously delicious honey in "Smashed". As this is Junji Ito, we are shown all the grisly details of a human being getting flattened to the thickness of a panini.   
*   _Witch Watch_: Nico's aptly named "Flip Flap Flat" spell transforms objects or people into paper-thin versions. In chapter 6 (anime episode 1), Nico demonstrates this magic on herself to impress Morihito, turning into a flattened, paper-thin sheet cutout. She instantly suffers severe side effects—blurred vision, lightness, vomiting confetti due to her body's inability to adapt—and gets swept away by the wind. Trapped in a narrow ditch too thin for rescue, she faces literal flattening death when the spell expires. Morihito barely saves her by smashing the surrounding wall seconds before she reverts.   
*   _Yakitate!! Japan_: Episode 15 features a bizarrely literal interpretation of "go get crushed," in which Tsukino willingly climbs into a hydraulic press and is flattened into a paper-thin state. She floats gently for a moment before being reinflated to her original form using a simple foot pump. The scene plays the absurdity completely straight, with no lasting physical consequences.
Asian Animation

## Examples:
*   _Gaju Bhai_: In "Tiku Thakela", Gaju's gang gets stuck on a hay cart rolling at high speed. Bhagat tries to stop the cart, only to be run over by it and flattened.   
*    In episode 37 of _Happy Superman Union_, a news report depicts Happy S. being squashed flat by a group of robots he has freed running right onto him.   
*   _Inspector Chingum_: In "Aakhri Ravan", a bunch of people run away and, not paying attention, step on Chingum in the process. Two other officers find him flattened afterward.   
*   _Motu Patlu (2012)_: In "Car Park", Motu and Patlu are flattened by Boxer's car running over them.   
*   _Nana Moon_: In episode 26, the gang are running through a secret hallway in Moon Haven's castle. Liz is caught in a trap involving a big hand on a spring that pushes her into the wall, flattening her. She's back to normal by the next shot where she's on-screen.   
*    In episode 55 of _Pleasant Goat and Big Big Wolf_, Jonie sits down and squashes Wolffy flat. She and the others then worry that Wolffy is dead; it later turns out he was just faking it.   
*   _Simple Samosa_:   
    *    In "Sumo Momo", one of the things Sumo Momo does to Samosa is to squash him flat and fold him into a paper airplane.   
    *    In "Spa Wars", as Iddiyappam Appa is chasing Samosa, he is squashed flat by Samosa using his remote to control one of the pieces of spa equipment. Appa is paper-thin for a few seconds after this, and then he inflates himself back to normal. 

*   _Zelly Go_: In "Rolling Ball", Gogo and Roro repeatedly get squashed flat by the jelly bean ball.
Comic Books

## Examples:
*   _Disney Ducks Comic Universe_: In a comic, Donald became a performance artist and one of his acts was getting squashed into a flat disc shape and being played on a gigantic gramophone.   
*   _Léonard le Génie_: When Basile operates a hydraulic press or similar tool, you can be 100% certain this will be the result.   
*   EC Comics: The _Vault of Horror_ story "Graft in Concrete!" (#26, Aug/Sep 1952) plays this lethally (though bloodlessly) straight.   
*   _JLA (1997)_: In #65 (June 2002), it happens to Plastic Man when his son (who has inherited his powers) becomes a bouncing Triceratops and lands on him.   
**Plastic Man:** Kids. Give 'em half a chance, and they'll walk all over you...

*   _Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds_: Trailing in last place, Cream uses the Monster Truck item to help clear a path for Tangle and her other friends, which results in her running over both Omega and Wave. Both are flat as pancakes, like in the game, Omega impressed with Cream's surprising penchant for motorvehicular violence. They both regain their regular shapes before crossing the finish line.
Comic Strips

## Examples:
*    One robber/rapist is crushed by a millstone in a story by Wilhelm Busch. Other than typical for this trope, he doesn't exactly revert.   
*    There's a Don Martin _MAD_ cartoon where two guys discover a friend lying in the road, completely flat and stretched out. Naturally they conclude that he has been run over by a steamroller, and proceed to _fold him up_ so they can take him to a hospital. Unfortunately due to a tragic misunderstanding involving a nearsighted strongman, he gets torn in half.   
*    This is an occasional outcome in _Spy vs. Spy._ Methods differ, including classics like the Anvil on Head, but a scenario involving quick-setting concrete and a steamroller has turned up before.   
*    The _Club Nintendo_ Halloween special had a brief scene where Mario slams a door on Kirby, flattening him. Link remarks "Oh man, this happens at least once in every comic," and then retrieves the bicycle pump. The scene in question can be seen here.   
*    The Narrowegians in the _Rufus Crustbuster_ comic strip of _Jack and Jill_ magazine were living pancake creatures who turned the title character into one with a machine.   
*   _U.S. Acres_: In an early strip, Orson's brothers do this to him when they "play squash".   
*   _Garfield_:   
    *    Happens to Garfield in one Sunday comic after he picks a fight with a larger cat. Jim Davis said he drew a rough sketch of Odie carrying home a flattened Garfield and thought it was so funny, he had to find a way to use it in an actual comic.   
    *    Nermal ends up flattened in one strip after Garfield accidentally sits on him.   
    *    Also a common fate for any spiders the fat ginger cat encounters. 

*   _The Far Side_: In one strip, a man gets squashed flat after getting trampled by an elephant, though his friend is more concerned about having made fun of his indestructible glasses earlier which survived being stomped.
Fan Works

## Examples:
*    Occurs several times in the _K.R.D. Chronicles_Series Fic of _Danganronpa_, with fatal results:   
    *   _Danganronpa: Memento Mori_: Ayane's execution at the end of Chapter 5 ends with her being crushed by a giant gavel, leaving her love interest Daigo covered in her blood.   
    *   _Danganronpa: Komm Susser Tod_: Sasuke is crushed under rubble at the end of Chapter 6, after he deliberately refuses to escape his Collapsing Lair.   
    *   _Danganronpa: Paradise Lost_: Goh is forced to weightlift several heavy objects during his execution in Chapter 4. Once a single feather is added, his arms break before he is subsequently crushed by the heap he was carrying. 

*   _The Disciple of Iroh (Star Wars)_: As a surprisingly fast Hutt weighing in excess of 900 kilos, Sorga isn't above literally sitting on opponents to dispatch them.   
    *    When Sorga hears a commotion outside his prison pit where some new pirate is threatening to shoot hostages and feed them to him, he decides to intervene and uses the Force to throw himself out through the hatch. He intends to land behind the pirate and send him flying... but when he doesn't see him at first, it takes Sorga a moment to realize that he misjudged his launch angle and landed directly _on_ the pirate.   
    *    A duelist bounty hunter interrupts the Disciples' morning meditation and demand to face Sorga right then and there, only to be beaten into the ground and used as a meditation platform by a ton of Hutt weight. 

## Examples:
*   _Here Comes the New Boss_: Played seriously at the Leviathan fight, where he seizes and crushes Assault, whose kinetic energy manipulation can deflect bullets but can't handle being surrounded and squashed in that way.   
*    In _No More_ Harry's accidental magic does it to him when he desperately wants to get out of his cupboard. He promptly proceeds to slide himself under the door.   
*   _Princess Maniacs_: At the end of the story, Pinky and the Brain are literally flattened for a few seconds after the Warner siblings accidentally step on the mice as the trio run towards and pile into the mice's Interdimensional Travel Device.   
*   Played for Drama in _The Secret Return of Alex Mack_, when Alex is trapped in her silvery form under the rubble of a collapsed building — for half a day, immobile and in blackness, until she's rescued. She develops Claustrophobia from the experience.   
*   _Vow of Nudity_: In the flashback narrative of _Showdown at Surly Gulch_, the slave H-B32 attempts suicide via this, standing under the outpost's steam hammer after the commander burns the only piece of paper that could have revealed to her what her real name is. The commander's son talks her out of following through at the very last moment.   
*    In the _What If Pokémon Sword & Shield Anime_, in SWSH133, Ash's Snorlax defeats Marnie's Toxicroak with a Body Slam, thus resulting in this happening to Marnie's Toxicroak.
Films — Animation

## Examples:
*   _Brave_: Mor'du dies at the climax when Queen Elinor pushes him into a stone pillar which collapses on him, killing him instantly and leaving only his paw poking out from beneath the ruin.   
*    Darla in _Cats Don't Dance_, who gets pressed into a table shape during the finale.   
*    In _Flushed Away_, in one of the times that Rita Malone's house tilts, multiple rats all land on one another as they hit the wall, and all peel off afterwards.   
*    In DreamWorks' _Home_, Pig the cat gets flattened against a car window.   
*    In Pixar's _Hoppers_, this is how the Insect Queen dies under the literal hands of Mabel Tanaka, whom she constantly attacks for defying her suggestion to (ironically) "squish" Mayor Jerry Generazzo in retaliation for endangering the environment.   
*    Count Dracula, during the credits sequence of _Hotel Transylvania_, is crushed into a heap after Frankenstein trips and falls on top of him.   
*   _Ice Age_:   
    *    In the first film, Scrat gets stepped on by several large animals but doesn't exactly get flattened, per se.   
    *    Squint receives this in _Continental Drift_, upon being stepped on by Ellie the mammoth. 

*    In _The Incredibles_, Helen Parr/Elastigirl's elasticity powers allow her to willingly compress her body to a minimum thickness of 1mm, and thus navigate impossibly tight spaces.   
    *    In the first film, while infiltrating Syndrome's base, she narrowly avoids being struck by an oncoming railpod in a tunnel by pressing herself paper-thin against the wall.   
    *    Elastigirl does this again in the sequel, when she flattens herself to slip through a narrow tunnel while riding atop a speeding train, emerging unscathed. 

## Examples:
*    By the end of _Kung Fu Panda 2_, Lord Shen met his maker when his own cannon fell on him.   
*   _Long Live Servatius_: Happens to the tiger after Servatius runs him over with a tank. However, the tiger survives it and remains alive for several decades as a pelt.   
*    In _Norm of the North_, one of the lemmings gets flattened in one part. In another part, two lemmings get flattened into the sides of a third one, who is squished as well.   
*    This is what happens to the letter I in Pixar's production logo, being crushed underneath a lamp.   
*   _Tiny Toon Adventures: How I Spent My Vacation_:   
    *    In Plucky's subplot, the Pig family is on their way to the HappyWorldLand amusement park, and Plucky, wanting to go with them, tries to stop their car by disguising himself as a construction worker and putting up many barriers. The Pig family's car's pedometer is about to reach 100,000 miles, and the Pig family is distracted with recording it, causing their car to run over Plucky, resulting in this trope. It then turns out that Wade forgot to take the lens cap off, so he backs the car up to try again, flattening Plucky twice more.   
**Plucky:** I think the left front tire is a little low.

    *    In Fifi's subplot, Fifi disguises herself as a star's manager to see him and annoys the actual manager. The woman, whose butt alone is bigger than Fifi is, responds by sitting on her. 

## Examples:
*   _Toast of London_: The main character has a flashback about the last encounter with his ex-wife where she runs him over with a steamroller.   
*   _The Two Ronnies_. In a spoof of _The Professionals_, a gun-waving Doyle kicks open a door, searches an apartment and is surprised to find no-one there. As he closes the door behind him, a flattened villain (represented by a squashed rubber dummy) falls out from behind it.   
*   _Ultraman Taro_: One episode guest-starring Ultraman Jack have this happening to the latter, after poor Jack got his chest timer removed resulting in him deflating to a flat form. He goes back to normal at the end of the episode.   
*    On _Whose Line Is It Anyway?_, one session of _Party Quirks_ involves Wayne Brady as "assorted celebrities being run over by a steamroller", sans cartoon effects of course. At one point he impersonates Gary Coleman, and gets squashed flat much quicker.
Manhua
*   _Old Master Q_ have this as a Running Gag as various Amusing Injuries the characters could get.   
    *    One of the strips sees Master Q and Big Potato discussing about Chin's new job, a circus elephant trainer, and decide to see how he's doing. Turns out Chin is a two-dimensional figure on the floor.   
    *    Another strip has Master Q being the elephant trainer instead, teaching the elephant to jump while holding the hoop _right in front of him_. The elephant jumps, and guess what happens next.
Multiple Media
*   _MonsterVerse_:   
    *   _Kong: Skull Island_: Colonel Packard is Killed Mid-Sentence near the film's end when Kong crushes the General Ripper to the ground with his fist in retaliation for Packard's effort to kill him.   
    *   _Godzilla: King of the Monsters (2019)_: During Ghidorah's Big Entrance awakening in Antarctica, one or two of the fleeing soldiers are visible being squashed by falling ice boulders when Ghidorah rips its wings free of the ice.   
    *   _Skull Island (2023)_: Hiro is violently crushed to death by the Kraken's tentacle in the first episode. In front of his son no less.
Music

## Examples:
*    Happens to Hall & Oates in the video for "Out Of Touch" after the two are run over by a giant drum rolling on its side.   
*    Happens to the girl in The Cars' video for "You Might Think" after singer/guitarist Ric Ocasek literally runs her over with a car during the line "You might think I'm delirious, the way I run you down".   
*    The music video for the D12 song "My Band" shows Swift being squashed flat after he wrestles the mic from Eminem and gets trampled by the audience.   
*    The Kid Laroi's music video "Thousand Miles" he gets run over by a steamroller driven by an evil version of himself.
Podcasts
*   _Bleeker Trails_: At the very end of episode 9, Moni gets a whale dropped on her at terminal velocity shortly after escaping the strange prehistoric beach, taking 2D10 damage as it hits the mountain and explodes. The episode promptly ends before it's revealed whether she miraculously survived or was killed, but Bridgett's indignant reaction indicates it was the latter. Episode 10 reveals that she survived, but was seriously injured.
Radio
*    In _The Goon Show_, Seagoon gets run over by a steamroller:   
**Seagoon:** The weight of the steamroller had made a lasting impression on me. I was now 2 inches thick and 24 feet wide. This was very awkward. People kept opening and shutting me.
Theater
*    This has been done before many times on magic shows, mostly to women. Here's an example.   
*    The Pantomime take on _Aladdin_ often features a scene at the Dame's laundry with the Butt-Monkey, getting caught in the wringer used to dry the clothes.
Theme Parks
*   _The Funtastic World of Hanna-Barbera_ at Universal Studios had this occur to Dick Dastardly and Muttley after they get crushed by an amusement park ride.
Video Games

## Examples:
*    In _Aladdin: Nasira's Revenge_, Aladdin gets flattened when heavy things fall on him.   
*    In _American McGee's Alice_, the White Rabbit is stomped to death by the Mad Hatter while helping a shrunken Alice safely get to the Caterpillar.   
*   _Banjo-Tooie_:   
    *    Getting crushed by Stomponadon's feet in Terrydactyland, a crusher in the Trash Compactor area in Grunty Industries, or Weldar's Ground Pound during his boss battle (also in Grunty Industries), has this effect; and it takes several seconds for Banjo (or whoever got crushed) to get back to the usual form and size. And in all cases, due to the strength of the impact, the life meter is reduced to only one unit, so getting crushed again immediately after will spell death.   
    *    The fate of Gruntilda's sisters when they lose to Banjo and Kazooie in the _Tower of Tragedy_ mini-game is getting crushed by large weights, which dangle over their (and Banjo and Kazooie’s) heads. 

## Examples:
*    When Rook takes King by checkmate in _Battle Chess_. In one blow, the Rook turns the King into the dimensions of a piece of paper, picks him up, and lets his flattened carcass float to the ground.   
*    Happens in _Battletoads_ if something heavy such as a boss lands on a toad.   
*    Happens to _Bayonetta_ if she is squashed by a Golem's ball form, or by the ice balls from the final boss. However, this only applies to the first game. There is nothing round that can land on her in the second game, due to its more serious nature. In the third game, however, Jeanne can get like this if she is crushed by an elevator.   
*    Given that the player commonly rolls eggs around, enemies in _Billy Hatcher and the Giant Egg_ will always suffer this fate.   
*    Happens in one death scene in _Brain Dead 13_ when the giant Living Statue squashes Lance with its big hand and spreads his... paint mess... on its body. This will also happen if Lance doesn't dodge Moose's shoulder charge.   
*    Happens to _Bug_ if he gets crushed by Smashing Hallway Traps of Doom, gets hit by a boulder, or if he falls off the terrain. If it was non-lethal, he stretches himself using a hand.   
*   _Cel Damage_, a game that runs entirely on cartoon physics, has this happens to anyone who gets hit with B.T. Bruno's sledgehammer, gets crushed by the 100-ton weight, or gets sucked through the vacuum.   
*    Happens to the enemies (Or your party) in _Chrono Cross_ when the summon Golem is cast.   
*   _Conker's Bad Fur Day_ puts a violent twist on this. If Conker is squished, he bleeds in addition to being flattened in cartoon fashion.   
*   _Crash Bandicoot_ series:   
    *    In the first game, Crash gets flattened if he gets hit by a stone wheel in "Jungle Rollers" and "Rolling Stones", by a boulder in "Boulders" and "Boulder Dash", or the barrels in "Toxic Waste", then he pulls himself up for a few seconds before falling back down.   

## Examples:
    *    In the second and third games, he can get crushed by the falling stone mechanisms in the ice levels of the former and the stone blocks dropped by some of the Mooks in the Egyptian levels of the latter. If he doesn't have an Aku Aku on him, he'll walk around crushed into just his head and feet, but if he does he'll spring back into shape. He can also get crushed by the triceratops in the prehistoric levels, and in the Egyptian levels can get crushed by the mummies while they're in their sarcophagus and flattened vertically by the moving walls.   
    *    In _Crash Team Racing_, _Crash Nitro Kart_, and _Crash Team Racing Nitro-Fueled_, a driver can be flattened by being run over by another driver using a Boost or Super Engine powerup or by track hazards like the toxic waste barrels on Sewer Speedway and the hammer-swinging statues on Thunder Struck.   
    *    In _Crash Tag Team Racing_, one of the Die-O-Ramas has Crash spinning into one of the two chicken news reporters who document the events of the game, who then punches him flat and kicks him offscreen. 

## Examples:
    *   Happens twice in "Feeling Pinkie Keen" to Twilight Sparkle with a door.◊ (Sort of. Once she peels herself off, she retains her shape with no inflation, as if her body only went into the door.)   
    *    In "Luna Eclipsed", Fluttershy pancakes herself on the door of her house when Twilight closes it all of a sudden.   
    *    In "Fame and Misfortune", Twilight is once again flattened by a door, this time courtesy of a stressed-out Applejack. 

## Examples:
*    Buford is subjected to this in the _Numb Chucks_ episode "Intelligence Not Included," after being run over by a steamroller.   
*    In _Oggy and the Cockroaches_, this is usually the fate of the cockroaches.   
*   _The Owl House_: The Greater Basilisk is ultimately defeated when Luz and the Troublemakers drop it several stories down through the dimensional doors from the Troublemakers' detention hideout back to the school stage and then dump several sandbags onto the top of it, popping the monster like a balloon and releasing its stolen magical energy.   
*   _Peanuts_: This happens to Woodstock in the special "A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving" while attempting to play basketball with Snoopy.   
*   _The Perils of Penelope Pitstop_: The Hooded Claw gets flattened by a huge dough kneader in a fortune cookie factory at the conclusion of "Bad Fortune in a Chinese Fortune Cookie."   
*    In _Pluto's Judgement Day_, one of the witnesses at Pluto's trial is a cat the dog chased under a steamroller, flattening him like a pancake. Even **his balloon** is flat!   
*    Implied then averted in the _Popeye_ cartoon "Nurse To Meet Ya," where Popeye and Bluto are trying to deliberately injure themselves so they can be with nurse Olive at the hospital. Popeye lies in the middle of the street waiting for a steamroller ("Get the syrup, nursie...I'm gonna be flat as a pancake!") only to be scooped up at the last moment by a street cleaner.   
*    Buttercup becomes this in the _The Powerpuff Girls (1998)_ episode "Down n' Dirty", and Bubbles and Buttercup are squished together in the episode "A Made Up Story".   
*   _Rainbow Butterfly Unicorn Kitty_: In "Anubis Newbie", Miguel is flattened between two pieces of wall during one of his attempts at completing a Death Course.   

## Examples:
*   _Razzberry Jazzberry Jam_: In "Jazzberries Unplugged", Buddy and Krupa are flattened after one of The Shock's many, many gigantic amps falls on them. The Shock then scrapes them up, folds them into a paper airplane, and throws them (they were standing on the House Of Jam's roof at the time; and hey, it does get them to the first floor faster than taking the stairs.) As to be expected from cartoon physics, they're back to full three-dimensionality the next time we see them.   
*    In _The Real Adventures of Jonny Quest_, this trope is Played for Horror. Although not shown, and for very good reason, a few scientists meet their end this way. It's obvious from Race's expression, and how soon he closes the door, that this was not a pretty way to go out.   
*   _Robot Chicken_: In the segment "Mighty Tubby Power Rangers", Dipsy, Lala, and Tinky Winky get stepped on by a giant monster. It's fatal.   
*   _Rocko's Modern Life_: Rocko is flattened on a regular basis.   
*   _Sonic the Hedgehog_ cartoons:   
    *    Happens many times in _Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog_, usually to Scratch and Grounder. One such example occurs during the episode, "The Mystery of the Missing Hi-Tops", when Scratch and Grounder manage to flatten themselves with their own steamroller. Their flattened selves float into an envelope that Sonic holds, then drops into a mailbox, declaring it, "junk mail".   
    *    Happens to Sonic himself in "Robotnikland" when Robotnik has trapped him in a regular theme park that's been converted into an Amusement Park of Doom. He attempts to escape by burrowing through the ground, only to quickly find that the concrete flooring has been reinforced, flattening him into a circle.   
    *    In "Ro-Becca", one of the comedy-focused episodes of _Sonic the Hedgehog (SatAM)_, Sonic and Rotor knock down a door that Antoine was standing behind. As they leave, the door goes back up, and we find that Antoine got flattened. 

## Examples:
*    In the _South Park_ episode "Fingerbang", Kenny dies by getting squashed by an elevator. His flat, bloody remains are then scraped off the bottom of it. Kenny has been squashed dead several times, mostly by cars.   
*   _Spliced_: In "Sgt. Snuggums", Peri and Entrée are flattened by a bunch of whirrels that Fuzzy throws onto them.   
*    This has happened a few times in _SpongeBob SquarePants_. One of the most notable instances being in the episode "Hall Monitor", when Patrick unknowingly lands on SpongeBob, flattening him.   
*   _Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2012)_: Michelangelo in "The Weird World of Wyrm," after the eponymous Reality Warper hits him with a hammer.   
*   _Teen Titans Go!_ has this happen to Robin after getting body slammed by Mammoth in "Gorilla". Starfire and Raven also do it by themselves while Robin is shouting at them at the end of the episode. For some reason.  
*   Tex Avery naturally loved the trope. "The Early Bird Dood It" gets bonus points for Flat Cat doing an Euler disk.   
*   _Tickety Toc_: In the episode _Watermelon Time_, Tooteroo gets flattened after being ran over by a large pumpkin rolling down a hill, he quickly pops up back to normal however.   
*    In one episode of _Timon & Pumbaa_, Timon is flattened after Pumbaa jumps on him. Another episode has a large flying squirrel crash into Timon and smash into a tree, flattening him underneath her. There is even an indent in the tree where she landed. FYI, there was no part of Timon, save his arms, that wasn't between her and the tree. There is also a weird _kissing_ sound effect for a few moments before she unpeels herself from the tree.   
*   _Tom and Jerry_ does this a lot, also putting variations on it.   
    *    In the last part of "Professor Tom", Tom runs at full speed to enter back the house in order to capture Jerry; when Jerry sees Tom come at him and runs away, Topsy approaches the door and opens it, resulting in Tom running over him and leaving him squashed flat.   

## Examples:
    *    At one point in "Love That Pup", Tom lures Spike (who's a sleeper) away with a steak suspended in a clothesline. Jerry does everything he can to try to wake up the dog, to no avail. His last resort is to stand in front of him with a stop gesture, only to get squashed by the dog as he continues walking forward to follow the scent of the steak.   
    *    In "Jerry and the Goldfish", when Tom tries to eat Goldie after putting her inside a toaster and trapping her between two sandwich slices, Jerry grabs his tail dna pulls it into a clothes roller, dragging Tom and leaving his body (and the toaster) completely flat like a towel.   
    *    Early in "Cruise Cat", Jerry tries to board the cruiser by walking through one of the ropes that keep the big vehicle aground. He then notices Tom is unfazedly grabbing the rope from the inner end, which leads to Jerry trying to run back to the pier, only for Tom to shake the rope so the resulting wave squashes Jerry just when he reaches the outer end.   
    *    Halfway during "Two Little Indians", the two eponymous mice approach Tom when the latter seizes Jerry, but the cat grabs a fly swatter and squashes both of them with it, forcing them to retreat.   
    *    In "Pup on a Picnic", upon being sneezed at full speed by Spike and bouncing back at him by a wire fence, Tom grabs the dog's basket as he quickly flies by, only to crash into a tree. Due to the impact, Tom knocks out part of the trunk and stops right between the tree's base and the upper part, getting crushed in the process and having his whole body flattened.   
    *    In "Muscle Beach Tom", the eponymous cat gets flattened after crashing onto a pillar, breaking off a portion in the middle so that the top crushes him into the shape of a crab.

Although, Dodon Pa also states that he _will_ directly invite Eggman for the next racing tournament.

That doesn't stop the doctor from crashing the party, and Dodon Pa decides to let the other racers deal with it for the Art of Racing. After the incident is resolved, Dodon Pa makes it clear he _will_ be inviting Eggman and the likes of the Zeti to the races when he's ready.  
*   Group Picture Ending: After the race, Dodon Pa decides to take a photo of the lineup of racers to commemorate how perfect his first test went, but the heroes and rivals end up brushing against each other before the photo can be taken. The final panel of the one-shot is absolute chaos, as Omega opens fire for Amy getting too close to him, Amy about to hit him with her hammer, with Cream trying to hold the latter back. Cheese, Wave, and Rouge are shocked by Omega's arsenal going off, while Sonic and Jet are about to start an argument themselves. Storm is seen trying to apologize to Tails after he accidentally stepped on one of his tails, Tangle and Whisper are about to fight Storm for the faux pas, and Froggy has jumped on Knuckles' head in the background monitor. Shadow, having enough of this ridiculousness, decides to just leave.  
*   Ignored Enemy:  

## This one-shot contains examples of the following tropes:
    *    Jet tries to antagonize Sonic before the race starts, picking up where they left off and saying he's gonna be the one to beat Sonic. However, Sonic spots Shadow on the racetrack and tries to get a rise out of him, brushing off the hawk. Jet fumes at being ignored by Sonic and aims to take down Shadow first. Funnily enough, after the two tag team Sonic with a pair of items, they have some grudging respect for one another and form their own rivalry between each other.  
    *    Eggman is largely ignored by the other racers who aren't Tails, Amy, Tangle or Whisper, being too caught up in the race to really care about the danger he possesses.
*   I'm Standing Right Here: Not exactly standing in the same spot, but rather "I can still hear you since I'm on a floating monitor head." Sonic initially brushes off Knuckles' absence as him not being invited since he "hates fun." Knuckles, thanks to Dodon Pa's livestreaming the event, says he heard Sonic's snide remark, and tells him he _was_ invited: he's just sitting out the first race because he's helping Big look for Froggy.  
*   iPhony: The panel showing Dodon Pa looking at a computer is roughly based on Apple's macOS, as seen with the rectangular icons on the bottom and a recycle bin/trash icon in the bottom-right corner of his screen. The computer itself seems to be based on a Mac mini, as it's also attached to the back of Dodon Pa's monitor, except the Mac mini itself is shaped like a wheel.  
*   Jaw Drop: Storm’s jaw drops when Omega points his guns at his face.  
*   Leaning on the Fourth Wall:  
    *    During a live-reaction moment between Big, Dodon Pa, and Knuckles, Knuckles is seen leaning against Dodon Pa's panel box with a Sweat Drop.  
    *    After Cream manages to flatten both Wave and Omega using a Monster Truck, Tangle comments on how it allowed her, Whisper, and Cream to catch up, saying the item is "a little too good", likely reflecting how some players might feel about the Monster Truck and its function as a Comeback Mechanic.

## This one-shot contains examples of the following tropes:
*   Lightning Glare: After Storm gets repelled by Omega's Shield item, both Wave and Rouge share a laugh at the albatross' misfortune. However, upon hearing them share this laugh, the two resume their heated rivalry by glaring at each other, which produces a small blue spark between them.  
*   Made of Iron: Eggman ends up being right next to his bomb when it detonates, but is simply knocked out rather than dead.  
*   Malicious Misnaming: Jet, not thrilled that his rival, Sonic, is overlooking him and is instead trying to compete with Shadow, gets up in the black hedgehog's face and tells him he'll take him down before Sonic, calling him "Sadness the Hedgehog."  
*   Mythology Gag: The B-Cover for this one-shot takes inspiration from _Sonic Drift_'s own cover art◊, just with some added characters.  
*   Only in It for the Money: When Team Dark is shown to be invited to try out Dodon Pa's new racing machines, Rouge is enamored at the prospect of the invitation outlining a "priceless prize that is infinite in scope", and when she sees Omega and Storm beefing with each other, she quips that the prize will be all hers. She's one of people most heartbroken by the fact that the "prize" is just the "joy of racing", which is worthless to her.  
*   Pet the Dog:  
    *    Knuckles helps find Froggy along with Big, despite not having any obligations to do so and the fact it means he can't go racing with his friends.  
    *    During the Group Picture Ending, Storm accidentally steps on one of Tails’ tails, having a regretful look on his face, and seems to be trying to apologize.

## This one-shot contains examples of the following tropes:
*   Punching Bag of Hatred: It’s shown that Amy has a punching bag and keeps a drawing of Dr. Eggman’s face taped on it.  
*   The Rival: While Team Dark and the Babylon Rogues are usually this to Team Sonic, the two groups end up forming a rivalry with each other, rather than the latter. It's especially notable that they end up targetting _each other_ more than they do Sonic and Tails, or even Eggman.  
*   Running Gag: Everything Dodon Pa does is for "the Art of Racing", from ensuring that the competitors are strapped inside their vehicles, letting Eggman wreak havoc on the track, and much more, it quickly becomes apparent that he believes _anything_ can be used to improve it. The racers tire of Dodon Pa saying "the art of Racing" soon enough.  
*   Squashed Flat: Trailing in last place, Cream uses the Monster Truck item to help clear a path for Tangle and her other friends, which results in her running over both Omega and Wave. Both are flat as pancakes, like in the game, Omega impressed with Cream's surprising penchant for motorvehicular violence. They both regain their regular shapes before crossing the finish line.  
*   Sudden Video Game Moment: There are a few gags that are based on the gameplay of _CrossWorlds_, represented with UI elements from the game itself. After Tangle uses the Slime item, some of the comic panels are also covered in the same green goop, mimicking the Interface Screw the Slime does in-game. Omega in particular has to spin his head around to shake it off, which is also represented by a control stick spinning Action Command, which is how players can also quickly shake off the slime.  
*   Villain Ball: Eggman shows up with a bomb powerful enough to completely disrupt the race and potentially do serious damage, but he holds off on detonating it as he'd prefer to do it after he wins the race. This ends up biting him in the ass, as it gives Whisper, Tails and Tangle enough time to throw him off the track, his bomb denotating not far from him.  

## This one-shot contains examples of the following tropes:
*   Women Are Wiser: Lampshaded and then subverted. Upon seeing Shadow and Omega immediately get rowdy with Jet and Storm during the race, Rouge and Wave simply snark as they observe the chaos, but soon enough, the two start to trade barbs and seek to outdo one another just as fiercely as the boys do.  
*   Workout Fanservice: Amy (who receives her invitation upon finishing her daily boxercise routine) first appears in the one-shot wearing a midriff-baring tank top and short shorts, the former resembling the upper half of her standard outfit.  
*   Worthless Treasure Twist: Dodon Pa promises a "priceless prize" at the end of the race that is "infinite in scope", something that Rouge is quite invested in obtaining. At the end, all of the racers manage to get into a 12-way pile-up tie. When asked who won, Dodon Pa simply says they're all winners, and they've obtained the grand prize: the joy of racing, which he says is priceless and "infinite in scope", and that the conclusion was the best tie ever to be seen in a race. Evidently, almost everyone is disappointed at Dodon Pa's big reveal, especially Rouge and Wave.  
**Rouge:**_"The joy of racing"?_ That's worth nothing!
**Wave:** I will never, ever hear the end of this from Jet.

## This one-shot contains examples of the following tropes:
*   Written-In Absence: Downplayed. Despite both Knuckles and Big being a part of the game's roster, the two are not participating in the tie-in comic's race as Knuckles is helping Big find Froggy. Dodon Pa, however, is still broadcasting the event for them to watch, so the cast can see their reactions while they're on the sidelines and occasionally comment on what's happening. A footnote shows that the two did eventually find Froggy, with him shown sitting in Big's hands.  
*   You Are Better Than You Think You Are: Tangle gives Whisper some encouraging words when the wolf gets insecure and feels like she might be useless without her Variable Wispon.

## Examples:
*   _Pokémon the Series_:   
    *    The original series episode "Gluttonous Kabigon! Huge Panic!" (or "Snack Attack!" in the English dub), in which Snorlax would roll over and lay on some of the Pokemon trying to attack him. The sight of a flattened Victreebel trying to walk around while flat, and shrieking at the top of its lungs, is hysterical.   
    *    Happens to Pikachu in the _Advanced Battle_ episode "Solid As A Solrock!" During a Gym Battle set in a planetarium, Pikachu charges Solrock with his Quick Attack, but Solrock moves out of the way, and Pikachu slams right into a model planet. Moments later, Pikachu's flattened form peels out of the crater and drifts to the ground.   
    *    Pikachu suffers this again in the _Black and White_ episode "New Places, Familar Faces"; After James' Amoongus body slams him, he is left flattened in a small crater, and stunned long enough for Team Rocket to capture him.   
    *    In the _Sun and Moon_ episode "Pulling Out The Pokemon Base Pepper!", a Snorlax uses its Z-Move, Pulverizing Pancake, on Team Rocket's Wobuffet, reducing it to, well... a pancake. 

## Examples:
*   _Punirunes (2022)_: In the first episode, Yuka's father accidentally squishes Airun when he is rolling dough for bread. Airun, being a squishy Punirune, isn't hurt by it and reverts to its normal shape afterward.   
*    Ransack and Crumplezone suffer this fate in the _Transformers: Cybertron_ episodes "Race" and "Ambush" (after being dropped on by Dirt Boss in the former, and run over by Metroplex in the latter).   
*   _Voices in the Dark_: This is a danger you face when eating the ridiculously delicious honey in "Smashed". As this is Junji Ito, we are shown all the grisly details of a human being getting flattened to the thickness of a panini.   
*   _Witch Watch_: Nico's aptly named "Flip Flap Flat" spell transforms objects or people into paper-thin versions. In chapter 6 (anime episode 1), Nico demonstrates this magic on herself to impress Morihito, turning into a flattened, paper-thin sheet cutout. She instantly suffers severe side effects—blurred vision, lightness, vomiting confetti due to her body's inability to adapt—and gets swept away by the wind. Trapped in a narrow ditch too thin for rescue, she faces literal flattening death when the spell expires. Morihito barely saves her by smashing the surrounding wall seconds before she reverts.   
*   _Yakitate!! Japan_: Episode 15 features a bizarrely literal interpretation of "go get crushed," in which Tsukino willingly climbs into a hydraulic press and is flattened into a paper-thin state. She floats gently for a moment before being reinflated to her original form using a simple foot pump. The scene plays the absurdity completely straight, with no lasting physical consequences.
Asian Animation

## Examples:
*   _Gaju Bhai_: In "Tiku Thakela", Gaju's gang gets stuck on a hay cart rolling at high speed. Bhagat tries to stop the cart, only to be run over by it and flattened.   
*    In episode 37 of _Happy Superman Union_, a news report depicts Happy S. being squashed flat by a group of robots he has freed running right onto him.   
*   _Inspector Chingum_: In "Aakhri Ravan", a bunch of people run away and, not paying attention, step on Chingum in the process. Two other officers find him flattened afterward.   
*   _Motu Patlu (2012)_: In "Car Park", Motu and Patlu are flattened by Boxer's car running over them.   
*   _Nana Moon_: In episode 26, the gang are running through a secret hallway in Moon Haven's castle. Liz is caught in a trap involving a big hand on a spring that pushes her into the wall, flattening her. She's back to normal by the next shot where she's on-screen.   
*    In episode 55 of _Pleasant Goat and Big Big Wolf_, Jonie sits down and squashes Wolffy flat. She and the others then worry that Wolffy is dead; it later turns out he was just faking it.   
*   _Simple Samosa_:   
    *    In "Sumo Momo", one of the things Sumo Momo does to Samosa is to squash him flat and fold him into a paper airplane.   
    *    In "Spa Wars", as Iddiyappam Appa is chasing Samosa, he is squashed flat by Samosa using his remote to control one of the pieces of spa equipment. Appa is paper-thin for a few seconds after this, and then he inflates himself back to normal. 

*   _Zelly Go_: In "Rolling Ball", Gogo and Roro repeatedly get squashed flat by the jelly bean ball.
Comic Books

## Examples:
*   _Disney Ducks Comic Universe_: In a comic, Donald became a performance artist and one of his acts was getting squashed into a flat disc shape and being played on a gigantic gramophone.   
*   _Léonard le Génie_: When Basile operates a hydraulic press or similar tool, you can be 100% certain this will be the result.   
*   EC Comics: The _Vault of Horror_ story "Graft in Concrete!" (#26, Aug/Sep 1952) plays this lethally (though bloodlessly) straight.   
*   _JLA (1997)_: In #65 (June 2002), it happens to Plastic Man when his son (who has inherited his powers) becomes a bouncing Triceratops and lands on him.   
**Plastic Man:** Kids. Give 'em half a chance, and they'll walk all over you...

*   _Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds_: Trailing in last place, Cream uses the Monster Truck item to help clear a path for Tangle and her other friends, which results in her running over both Omega and Wave. Both are flat as pancakes, like in the game, Omega impressed with Cream's surprising penchant for motorvehicular violence. They both regain their regular shapes before crossing the finish line.
Comic Strips

## Examples:
*    One robber/rapist is crushed by a millstone in a story by Wilhelm Busch. Other than typical for this trope, he doesn't exactly revert.   
*    There's a Don Martin _MAD_ cartoon where two guys discover a friend lying in the road, completely flat and stretched out. Naturally they conclude that he has been run over by a steamroller, and proceed to _fold him up_ so they can take him to a hospital. Unfortunately due to a tragic misunderstanding involving a nearsighted strongman, he gets torn in half.   
*    This is an occasional outcome in _Spy vs. Spy._ Methods differ, including classics like the Anvil on Head, but a scenario involving quick-setting concrete and a steamroller has turned up before.   
*    The _Club Nintendo_ Halloween special had a brief scene where Mario slams a door on Kirby, flattening him. Link remarks "Oh man, this happens at least once in every comic," and then retrieves the bicycle pump. The scene in question can be seen here.   
*    The Narrowegians in the _Rufus Crustbuster_ comic strip of _Jack and Jill_ magazine were living pancake creatures who turned the title character into one with a machine.   
*   _U.S. Acres_: In an early strip, Orson's brothers do this to him when they "play squash".   
*   _Garfield_:   
    *    Happens to Garfield in one Sunday comic after he picks a fight with a larger cat. Jim Davis said he drew a rough sketch of Odie carrying home a flattened Garfield and thought it was so funny, he had to find a way to use it in an actual comic.   
    *    Nermal ends up flattened in one strip after Garfield accidentally sits on him.   
    *    Also a common fate for any spiders the fat ginger cat encounters. 

*   _The Far Side_: In one strip, a man gets squashed flat after getting trampled by an elephant, though his friend is more concerned about having made fun of his indestructible glasses earlier which survived being stomped.

*    The _Club Nintendo_ Halloween special had a brief scene where Mario slams a door on Kirby, flattening him. Link remarks "Oh man, this happens at least once in every comic," and then retrieves the bicycle pump. The scene in question can be seen here.   
*    The Narrowegians in the _Rufus Crustbuster_ comic strip of _Jack and Jill_ magazine were living pancake creatures who turned the title character into one with a machine.   
*   _U.S. Acres_: In an early strip, Orson's brothers do this to him when they "play squash".   
*   _Garfield_:   
    *    Happens to Garfield in one Sunday comic after he picks a fight with a larger cat. Jim Davis said he drew a rough sketch of Odie carrying home a flattened Garfield and thought it was so funny, he had to find a way to use it in an actual comic.   
    *    Nermal ends up flattened in one strip after Garfield accidentally sits on him.   
    *    Also a common fate for any spiders the fat ginger cat encounters. 

*   _The Far Side_: In one strip, a man gets squashed flat after getting trampled by an elephant, though his friend is more concerned about having made fun of his indestructible glasses earlier which survived being stomped.

*   The Gadfly: During the race, Omega points his gun at Storm when the two are neck and neck, causing both the latter and a nearby Rouge to think he's about to open fire on the Albatross... only for him to use this momentary surprise to use his Drill Wisp to speed ahead instead, satisfied with the reaction (though not satisfied with the amount of destruction he was able to wreak).  
*   Go-Karting with Bowser: Played With. Eggman arrives on the track which Sonic and company are already in the middle of racing, and while he's brought with him a bomb that's strong enough to make a mess of things, he decides he wants to hold off on detonation until he wins the race. Dodon Pa reveals he didn't invite the guy as much as Eggman saw the invites going out and intercepted them. Although, Dodon Pa also states that he _will_ directly invite Eggman for the next racing tournament.  
*   Good Is Not Dumb: Zig-zagged. While his methods for testing his vehicles are... questionable, Dodon Pa decided not to invite Eggman to this initial test race. That doesn't stop the doctor from crashing the party, and Dodon Pa decides to let the other racers deal with it for the Art of Racing. After the incident is resolved, Dodon Pa makes it clear he _will_ be inviting Eggman and the likes of the Zeti to the races when he's ready.  
*   Group Picture Ending: After the race, Dodon Pa decides to take a photo of the lineup of racers to commemorate how perfect his first test went, but the heroes and rivals end up brushing against each other before the photo can be taken. The final panel of the one-shot is absolute chaos, as Omega opens fire for Amy getting too close to him, Amy about to hit him with her hammer, with Cream trying to hold the latter back. Cheese, Wave, and Rouge are shocked by Omega's arsenal going off, while Sonic and Jet are about to start an argument themselves. Storm is seen trying to apologize to Tails after he accidentally stepped on one of his tails, Tangle and Whisper are about to fight Storm for the faux pas, and Froggy has jumped on Knuckles' head in the background monitor. Shadow, having enough of this ridiculousness, decides to just leave.

## This one-shot contains examples of the following tropes:
    *    Jet tries to antagonize Sonic before the race starts, picking up where they left off and saying he's gonna be the one to beat Sonic. However, Sonic spots Shadow on the racetrack and tries to get a rise out of him, brushing off the hawk. Jet fumes at being ignored by Sonic and aims to take down Shadow first. Funnily enough, after the two tag team Sonic with a pair of items, they have some grudging respect for one another and form their own rivalry between each other.  
    *    Eggman is largely ignored by the other racers who aren't Tails, Amy, Tangle or Whisper, being too caught up in the race to really care about the danger he possesses.
*   I'm Standing Right Here: Not exactly standing in the same spot, but rather "I can still hear you since I'm on a floating monitor head." Sonic initially brushes off Knuckles' absence as him not being invited since he "hates fun." Knuckles, thanks to Dodon Pa's livestreaming the event, says he heard Sonic's snide remark, and tells him he _was_ invited: he's just sitting out the first race because he's helping Big look for Froggy.  
*   iPhony: The panel showing Dodon Pa looking at a computer is roughly based on Apple's macOS, as seen with the rectangular icons on the bottom and a recycle bin/trash icon in the bottom-right corner of his screen. The computer itself seems to be based on a Mac mini, as it's also attached to the back of Dodon Pa's monitor, except the Mac mini itself is shaped like a wheel.  
*   Jaw Drop: Storm’s jaw drops when Omega points his guns at his face.  
*   Leaning on the Fourth Wall:  
    *    During a live-reaction moment between Big, Dodon Pa, and Knuckles, Knuckles is seen leaning against Dodon Pa's panel box with a Sweat Drop.  
    *    After Cream manages to flatten both Wave and Omega using a Monster Truck, Tangle comments on how it allowed her, Whisper, and Cream to catch up, saying the item is "a little too good", likely reflecting how some players might feel about the Monster Truck and its function as a Comeback Mechanic.

## This one-shot contains examples of the following tropes:
*   Lightning Glare: After Storm gets repelled by Omega's Shield item, both Wave and Rouge share a laugh at the albatross' misfortune. However, upon hearing them share this laugh, the two resume their heated rivalry by glaring at each other, which produces a small blue spark between them.  
*   Made of Iron: Eggman ends up being right next to his bomb when it detonates, but is simply knocked out rather than dead.  
*   Malicious Misnaming: Jet, not thrilled that his rival, Sonic, is overlooking him and is instead trying to compete with Shadow, gets up in the black hedgehog's face and tells him he'll take him down before Sonic, calling him "Sadness the Hedgehog."  
*   Mythology Gag: The B-Cover for this one-shot takes inspiration from _Sonic Drift_'s own cover art◊, just with some added characters.  
*   Only in It for the Money: When Team Dark is shown to be invited to try out Dodon Pa's new racing machines, Rouge is enamored at the prospect of the invitation outlining a "priceless prize that is infinite in scope", and when she sees Omega and Storm beefing with each other, she quips that the prize will be all hers. She's one of people most heartbroken by the fact that the "prize" is just the "joy of racing", which is worthless to her.  
*   Pet the Dog:  
    *    Knuckles helps find Froggy along with Big, despite not having any obligations to do so and the fact it means he can't go racing with his friends.  
    *    During the Group Picture Ending, Storm accidentally steps on one of Tails’ tails, having a regretful look on his face, and seems to be trying to apologize.

## This one-shot contains examples of the following tropes:
*   Punching Bag of Hatred: It’s shown that Amy has a punching bag and keeps a drawing of Dr. Eggman’s face taped on it.  
*   The Rival: While Team Dark and the Babylon Rogues are usually this to Team Sonic, the two groups end up forming a rivalry with each other, rather than the latter. It's especially notable that they end up targetting _each other_ more than they do Sonic and Tails, or even Eggman.  
*   Running Gag: Everything Dodon Pa does is for "the Art of Racing", from ensuring that the competitors are strapped inside their vehicles, letting Eggman wreak havoc on the track, and much more, it quickly becomes apparent that he believes _anything_ can be used to improve it. The racers tire of Dodon Pa saying "the art of Racing" soon enough.  
*   Squashed Flat: Trailing in last place, Cream uses the Monster Truck item to help clear a path for Tangle and her other friends, which results in her running over both Omega and Wave. Both are flat as pancakes, like in the game, Omega impressed with Cream's surprising penchant for motorvehicular violence. They both regain their regular shapes before crossing the finish line.  
*   Sudden Video Game Moment: There are a few gags that are based on the gameplay of _CrossWorlds_, represented with UI elements from the game itself. After Tangle uses the Slime item, some of the comic panels are also covered in the same green goop, mimicking the Interface Screw the Slime does in-game. Omega in particular has to spin his head around to shake it off, which is also represented by a control stick spinning Action Command, which is how players can also quickly shake off the slime.  
*   Villain Ball: Eggman shows up with a bomb powerful enough to completely disrupt the race and potentially do serious damage, but he holds off on detonating it as he'd prefer to do it after he wins the race. This ends up biting him in the ass, as it gives Whisper, Tails and Tangle enough time to throw him off the track, his bomb denotating not far from him.

## This one-shot contains examples of the following tropes:
*   Women Are Wiser: Lampshaded and then subverted. Upon seeing Shadow and Omega immediately get rowdy with Jet and Storm during the race, Rouge and Wave simply snark as they observe the chaos, but soon enough, the two start to trade barbs and seek to outdo one another just as fiercely as the boys do.  
*   Workout Fanservice: Amy (who receives her invitation upon finishing her daily boxercise routine) first appears in the one-shot wearing a midriff-baring tank top and short shorts, the former resembling the upper half of her standard outfit.  
*   Worthless Treasure Twist: Dodon Pa promises a "priceless prize" at the end of the race that is "infinite in scope", something that Rouge is quite invested in obtaining. At the end, all of the racers manage to get into a 12-way pile-up tie. When asked who won, Dodon Pa simply says they're all winners, and they've obtained the grand prize: the joy of racing, which he says is priceless and "infinite in scope", and that the conclusion was the best tie ever to be seen in a race. Evidently, almost everyone is disappointed at Dodon Pa's big reveal, especially Rouge and Wave.  
**Rouge:**_"The joy of racing"?_ That's worth nothing!
**Wave:** I will never, ever hear the end of this from Jet.

_**Farewell Concert**_ is the live recording of the band Cream's final concert at the Royal Albert Hall on 26 November 1968. Aside from the band's reunion concert in 2005 it is Cream's only official full concert release on video. It was originally broadcast by the BBC on 5 January 1969. It was not released on video in the US until 1977. The opening acts for the concert were future progressive rock stars Yes, who were just starting out, and Taste, an Irish trio led by Rory Gallagher.
There are in fact several versions of this film. They are as follows -
_**Original theatrical release**_
*   Created by Director Tony Palmer and distributed by manager Robert Stigwood, this was a documentary style film, incorporated live performances, narration by BBC announcer Patrick Allen, and interviews with the band members themselves showcasing their playing abilities (actually filmed in late 1967 or early 1968). Duration was 84 minutes._[citation needed_]  
*   In 1977, a shorter version of the above film, presenting the footage in edited form, now lasting 51 minutes, was released on home video.
_**Television version**_
*   The first BBC Television broadcast - Containing the same songs as the 1977 version (and lasting the same length), but featuring narration from Radio One DJ Pete Drummond, and a different introduction and BBC end credits. (Note - The narrations by both Drummond and Allen are virtually identical.) This was also on the official DVD release._[citation needed_]  
*   A music only version, shown by the BBC in 1980 (The end credits show "MCMLXXX"), which was 30 minutes long, featuring just five complete songs, with no narration or interviews.

In 2005, a _special extended edition_ of the concert appeared featuring full versions of all songs separated from the narration and interviews. Lasting 80 minutes, it was released on the official DVD reissue. The new version featured digitally remastered sound and video including three bonus songs. A short clip of White Room from the second set (the film used the version from the first show), together with D.J. John Peel introducing the band onstage, was shown on the BBC1 programme "The Rock And Roll Years" in the late 1980s.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell_Concert#cite_note-1)
In June 2014, it was given a Blu-ray / DVD release.
_**Album release**_ In March 2020, the concert was released as part of the live album _Goodbye Tour - Live 1968_, being the first time the Royal Albert Hall concert was officially released via audio format.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell_Concert#cite_note-2) The sound of this Royal Albert hall concert is much worse than the sound of the other 3 shows of this box set.
The original film has often been criticized for both its mediocre sound and visual effects:
> The audio is a turgid sonic sludge. The visuals are even worse, with director Tony Palmer jerking the camera around as if this were an episode of NYPD Blue, layering the picture with dated and distracting psychedelic light effects, and providing far too many close-ups of Bruce's teeth (and almost no wide shots of the entire band).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell_Concert#cite_note-3)

The band had performed two sets at the Albert Hall, but it is believed only the second set was filmed in its entirety. Several times during the performance, it is apparent that the on-screen shot is not in sync with the audio. In fact, in several songs, including during Ginger Baker's drum solo, he seems to change clothes at lightning speed due to careless post-editing, as well as Eric Clapton playing two different guitars. This is because footage from both sets, with the band wearing different clothes and Clapton using a Gibson Firebird for the first set, a Gibson 335 for the second, were edited together. The BBC used four static cameras and two hand held cams, all recording onto video tape, whilst Palmer himself filmed footage at the front of the stage, utilising a 16mm film camera. The difference in quality can be detected easily during the broadcast. However, the BBC "Pete Drummond" version was better quality overall, and is the only version that has these 16mm film clips removed – the remastered release on the 2005 DVD presents both audio and video in excellent quality._[citation needed_]
Ginger Baker himself has lashed out in an interview against the _Farewell Concert_ video, stating: "Cream was so much better than that." Nonetheless, most Cream fans regard the actual performance with great enthusiasm, disregarding the poor quality of the video.

# So This Is Goodbye: When Cream Said Farewell At The Royal Albert Hall
On November 26, 1968, Cream played their farewell concert at London’s Royal Albert Hall.
Published on November 26, 2025
By
Richard Havers
Cover: Courtesy of Universal Music
By 1968, London’s Royal Albert Hall was seen by most people as the UK’s home of classical music. Despite hosting concerts by the **Rolling Stones**, **The Beatles**, **Bob Dylan** and others over the previous five years, And while there had been rock concerts there before, there was never a rock concert as intense and as significant as the one on November 26, 1968, when **Cream** officially said farewell as a band.
In their two years of existence, the trio’s success had been phenomenal; they conquered America, fell out with one another and redefined what a rock trio with blues sensibilities could achieve. There is no band that followed Cream with a similar make-up that was not influenced by them. Cream became the template for heavy metal, and yet their respect for the blues and **Jack Bruce**’s huge musical talent for composition always gave them an edge over their rivals.

# Fan Faithfully Reconstructs Cream’s Final Concert: Watch a New Version of the Show with the Correct Song Order and Run-Time (1968)
in _Music_ | March 15th, 2022 4 Comments

The orig­i­nal rock super­group, Cream, last­ed two years, changed the course of rock music, bare­ly held togeth­er because of ran­cor between mem­bers and said good­bye in 1968. Their farewell con­cert at the Roy­al Albert Hall in Lon­don was one for the ages. Maybe not their best per­for­mance, but one of their most ener­getic. And inside the cav­ernous Hall, the three men laid down a wall of unde­ni­able sound.
Too bad that it wasn’t prop­er­ly doc­u­ment­ed, despite a series of cam­eras there that evening. A Youtube denizen called Mike Left­on has tried to rec­ti­fy the his­to­ry by assem­bling a cut of the 70-minute con­cert that plays in real time. It’s the kind of fan project for which YouTube is designed—something not pro­fes­sion­al enough for offi­cial release, but vital­ly impor­tant for the fans.

# Fan Faithfully Reconstructs Cream’s Final Concert: Watch a New Version of the Show with the Correct Song Order and Run-Time (1968)
Go on to the Bezos­Borg site (you know, it rhymes with Glama­zon), and you can find a con­cert film offered on Blu-Ray. What’s wrong with that, you might ask? Cream fans will tell you. Instead of let­ting the band play, the offi­cial Farewell Con­cert leaves off sev­er­al songs, and includes a “total­ly square voiceover by Patrick Allen (who refers to the band as “The Cream” through­out),” accord­ing to the moviesteve.com web­site, while anoth­er review­er notes this could be the gen­e­sis of Spinal Tap’s inten­tion­al­ly bad inter­views. (But let’s be fair, the 1960s in gen­er­al were filled with non-rock jour­nal­ists inter­view­ing musi­cians as if they were alien life forms. D.A. Pennebaker’s _Don’t Look Back_ is a com­pendi­um of such cringey moments.)
On top of that, direc­tor Allen real­ly over­did the zoom lens, which was every­where those days. It’s fun­ny to see how it was used to “spice up” rock band footage, where real­ly you could just hold the cam­era on Gin­ger Bak­er play­ing drums.

45 Years Ago: Cream Perform ‘Farewell Concert’
Dave Swanson
Dave SwansonPublished: November 26, 2013
George Stroud/Hulton Archive, Getty Images
*   Share on Facebook

After just over two years as a band, Cream gave their final performance on Nov. 26, 1968. The concert was held at the Royal Albert Hall In England. Cream's decision to disband took fans by surprise, though simmering tensions within the band, primarily between Jack Bruce and Ginger Baker, came to a head, as Eric Clapton was losing interest in the band. They embarked on a 'farewell tour' of 19 cities in the U.S. before the two-night stand finale, Nov. 25 & 26, at the Royal Albert Hall.
The concerts were recorded and broadcast by the BBC in early 1969. The recordings were to serve as part of the band's final album. Planned as a double album, with half recorded live and half in the studio, the idea was scrapped in favor of a single LP with one side live and one side previously unissued studio material. Issued as 'Goodbye,' the live selections were taken from a show at the L.A. Fourm. A concert film followed a decade later.

# 45 Years Ago: Cream Perform ‘Farewell Concert’
The band were apparently unhappy with those final shows and even die hard fans admit it wasn't the band at the peak of their powers. In the documentary, 'Cream: Classic Artists,' Baker said "It wasn’t a good gig. Cream was better than that. We knew it was all over, we knew we were just finishing it off."
Opening acts on the various tour dates included Rory Gallagher's Taste, Deep Purple and the newly formed Yes. Cream finally reunited in 2005 for a series of shows in the UK and US, which were a huge critical and financial success.

How could a band last for a little over two years, be so successful, and then break up? In fact, what they were doing was setting a template of another kind. The whole business of supergroups was to prove to be the thing in the 70s, starting with **Blind Faith**, which **Eric Clapton** and Baker formed with **Steve Winwood** and Ric Grech in early 1969.

After just over two years as a band, Cream gave their final performance on Nov. 26, 1968. The concert was held at the Royal Albert Hall In England. Cream's decision to disband took fans by surprise, though simmering tensions within the band, primarily between Jack Bruce and Ginger Baker, came to a head, as Eric Clapton was losing interest in the band. They embarked on a 'farewell tour' of 19 cities in the U.S. before the two-night stand finale, Nov. 25 & 26, at the Royal Albert Hall.
The concerts were recorded and broadcast by the BBC in early 1969. The recordings were to serve as part of the band's final album. Planned as a double album, with half recorded live and half in the studio, the idea was scrapped in favor of a single LP with one side live and one side previously unissued studio material. Issued as 'Goodbye,' the live selections were taken from a show at the L.A. Fourm. A concert film followed a decade later.

# 45 Years Ago: Cream Perform ‘Farewell Concert’
The band were apparently unhappy with those final shows and even die hard fans admit it wasn't the band at the peak of their powers. In the documentary, 'Cream: Classic Artists,' Baker said "It wasn’t a good gig. Cream was better than that. We knew it was all over, we knew we were just finishing it off."
Opening acts on the various tour dates included Rory Gallagher's Taste, Deep Purple and the newly formed Yes. Cream finally reunited in 2005 for a series of shows in the UK and US, which were a huge critical and financial success.

_**Farewell Concert**_ is the live recording of the band Cream's final concert at the Royal Albert Hall on 26 November 1968. Aside from the band's reunion concert in 2005 it is Cream's only official full concert release on video. It was originally broadcast by the BBC on 5 January 1969. It was not released on video in the US until 1977. The opening acts for the concert were future progressive rock stars Yes, who were just starting out, and Taste, an Irish trio led by Rory Gallagher.
There are in fact several versions of this film. They are as follows -
_**Original theatrical release**_
*   Created by Director Tony Palmer and distributed by manager Robert Stigwood, this was a documentary style film, incorporated live performances, narration by BBC announcer Patrick Allen, and interviews with the band members themselves showcasing their playing abilities (actually filmed in late 1967 or early 1968). Duration was 84 minutes._[citation needed_]  
*   In 1977, a shorter version of the above film, presenting the footage in edited form, now lasting 51 minutes, was released on home video.
_**Television version**_
*   The first BBC Television broadcast - Containing the same songs as the 1977 version (and lasting the same length), but featuring narration from Radio One DJ Pete Drummond, and a different introduction and BBC end credits. (Note - The narrations by both Drummond and Allen are virtually identical.) This was also on the official DVD release._[citation needed_]  
*   A music only version, shown by the BBC in 1980 (The end credits show "MCMLXXX"), which was 30 minutes long, featuring just five complete songs, with no narration or interviews.
texts.1:
In 2005, a _special extended edition_ of the concert appeared featuring full versions of all songs separated from the narration and interviews. Lasting 80 minutes, it was released on the official DVD reissue. The new version featured digitally remastered sound and video including three bonus songs. A short clip of White Room from the second set (the film used the version from the first show), together with D.J. John Peel introducing the band onstage, was shown on the BBC1 programme "The Rock And Roll Years" in the late 1980s.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell_Concert#cite_note-1)
In June 2014, it was given a Blu-ray / DVD release.
_**Album release**_ In March 2020, the concert was released as part of the live album _Goodbye Tour - Live 1968_, being the first time the Royal Albert Hall concert was officially released via audio format.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell_Concert#cite_note-2) The sound of this Royal Albert hall concert is much worse than the sound of the other 3 shows of this box set.
The original film has often been criticized for both its mediocre sound and visual effects:
> The audio is a turgid sonic sludge. The visuals are even worse, with director Tony Palmer jerking the camera around as if this were an episode of NYPD Blue, layering the picture with dated and distracting psychedelic light effects, and providing far too many close-ups of Bruce's teeth (and almost no wide shots of the entire band).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell_Concert#cite_note-3)
texts.2:
The band had performed two sets at the Albert Hall, but it is believed only the second set was filmed in its entirety. Several times during the performance, it is apparent that the on-screen shot is not in sync with the audio. In fact, in several songs, including during Ginger Baker's drum solo, he seems to change clothes at lightning speed due to careless post-editing, as well as Eric Clapton playing two different guitars. This is because footage from both sets, with the band wearing different clothes and Clapton using a Gibson Firebird for the first set, a Gibson 335 for the second, were edited together. The BBC used four static cameras and two hand held cams, all recording onto video tape, whilst Palmer himself filmed footage at the front of the stage, utilising a 16mm film camera. The difference in quality can be detected easily during the broadcast. However, the BBC "Pete Drummond" version was better quality overall, and is the only version that has these 16mm film clips removed – the remastered release on the 2005 DVD presents both audio and video in excellent quality._[citation needed_]
Ginger Baker himself has lashed out in an interview against the _Farewell Concert_ video, stating: "Cream was so much better than that." Nonetheless, most Cream fans regard the actual performance with great enthusiasm, disregarding the poor quality of the video.
